warning: THE LABELLERS DO NOT OPEN THIS FILE. It maps each blinded id back to its title, its place in that title and which detectors proposed it. Opening it before labelling would unblind the review and waste the whole exercise.
titles_need_every_candidate_list: a title joins the pool only when every list above has analysed it. A title only one of them has seen has no unflagged time in the sense this pool means, because the other lists never had the chance to flag it.

iris_build.note: built against Homebrew's OpenCV and ffmpeg rather than the vcpkg versions upstream pins, because the Docker build could not be run on this machine. docs/DECISIONS.md carries the deviation and eval/baselines/iris/README.md says what it costs.

candidate_lists_note: every list the plan asks for has run. EA IRIS used to be missing, and while it was, anything only IRIS would have caught was not in the union, which made this pool's recall estimate optimistic by an unknown amount. It is in now, built natively rather than in Docker, and `iris_build` says which build it was.
theora_rescreen: the four Theora .ogv titles failed to decode in the first screening run, with avcodec_send_packet returning 22, so their windows came from the two ffmpeg based lists only. flashmap's Theora decoding was fixed (see flashmap/tests/test_theora.py), the four titles were screened again on 2026-09-17, and this pool was cut from that merged result. results/screening.json records the re-run under `rescreens`. One of the four, the Malaysia night pass, is shorter than a single segment and is skipped for that reason rather than for the decoder.
rebuilding_this_pool: a segment id is a position in a shuffled list, so rebuilding after labelling has begun leaves the answers pointing at different segments. make_pool refuses while any sheet has an answer in it, and the plot run deletes a figure before re-rendering it so no figure from an earlier pool can survive under a new id.
